# Russia’s Fuel Crisis Spirals As Ukraine Strikes Oil Sites

Published

Jul 01, 2026 at 10:00 AM EDT

![Ellie Cook](https://assets.newsweek.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/2187938-ellie-cook.png?w=1600&quality=80&webp=1)

Senior Reporter

Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil facilities are paying off—so much so, even Russian President Vladimir Putin can't ignore how effective Ukraine's pressure campaign has become.

"Unfortunately, there are still queues at petrol stations, and finding the right grade of petrol isn't always easy," Putin said in a meeting with oil executives and top government officials over the weekend.

"Problems persist for both motorists and businesses," the Russian leader added, according to a Kremlin readout.

#### Read More on World

Putin's remarks are a rare public acknowledgment of the strain Ukraine's dogged targeting of Russia's oil and gas facilities is putting on Moscow as Kyiv tries to make it more expensive for Russia to continue its war effort.

Russia is a major oil exporter and relies on this revenue to keep its economy going, especially because it dedicates so much of government spending to the military. Russia's army also needs fuel to make sure it can sustain its tanks, armored vehicles and logistics operations in south and eastern Ukraine.

![Cars line up at a Lukoil gas station in Moscow, Tuesday, June 30, 2026.](https://assets.newsweek.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/AP26181606929718-1.jpg?w=1600&quality=80&webp=1)

# Anthropic Tightens Controls Over Model Access

||By [LDS Team](/editorial-standards)

8.0

Relevance Score

![Anthropic Tightens Controls Over Model Access](https://gizmodo.com/app/uploads/2026/07/DarioAmodei-1200x675.jpg)

Photo: gizmodo.com [· rights & takedowns](/copyright)

Anthropic is rolling back a hidden mechanism in **Claude Code** that secretly flagged users tied to China by checking system timezone against Asia/Shanghai or Asia/Urumqi and scanning proxy URLs, active since an **April 2, 2026** release. Anthropic engineer **Thariq Shihipar** said the check was "an experiment we launched in March" meant to prevent account abuse and distillation, and confirmed it will be fully removed in the next update. The disclosure follows a U.S. Commerce Department export-control order that forced Anthropic to briefly disable **Fable 5** and **Mythos 5** for foreign nationals in mid-June, an episode triggered by an Amazon-reported jailbreak that reached the White House. For practitioners, it signals that geopolitical access controls and metadata-based user screening are becoming routine engineering and compliance requirements for teams deploying frontier AI tools globally.

For AI platform and security
